statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Each of NRS 176A.245, 176A.265, and 176A.295 has two mechanisms. Subsection 1 directs the applicable court to seal qualifying records after discharge from probation or dismissal under the corresponding treatment program, without a participant filing and without a hearing unless the Division petitions for good cause not to seal and requests a hearing. Subsection 2 requires a defendant's petition, not sooner than seven years after conditional dismissal or setting aside of judgment, for a charge under NRS 200.485, NRS 484C.110, or NRS 484C.120. Subsection 3 bars relief for charges under NRS 200.508 or NRS 200.5099.
doNotImport: Do not import the ordinary NRS 179.245 petition, its sample pleadings, or its process into this route.
Do not apply the NRS 179.245(9) sex-trafficking fee waiver to a petition under NRS 176A.245, NRS 176A.265, or NRS 176A.295.
Do not invent a statewide filing fee, waiver form, service recipient, service method, or proposed-order practice where the approved route record preserves those as local questions.
Do not describe Nevada record sealing as expungement, destruction of records, restoration of firearm rights, or relief reaching federal, tribal, military, or out-of-state records.

documents.title: The Question That Decides Whether Anything Is Filed

sections.heading: Subsection 1 or subsection 2
sections.body:
ONE QUESTION decides whether anything in this packet is filed:

Were you charged with a violation of NRS 200.485 (battery constituting domestic violence), NRS 484C.110 or NRS 484C.120 (driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle under the influence, or the related controlled-substance driving offence), AND were the charges conditionally dismissed or the judgment of conviction set aside?

IF NO — subsection 1 of the applicable section applies. Sealing is AUTOMATIC: after you are discharged from probation or the case is dismissed under the programme section, the court shall order the records sealed, without a hearing, if you fulfilled the terms and conditions imposed by the court and the Division — unless the Division petitions the court, for good cause shown, not to seal and requests a hearing. You file NOTHING. Do not file the petition in this packet. The referral page says where to go instead.

IF YES — subsection 2 applies. Sealing is NOT automatic: it follows only upon the filing of a petition by you, and the petition cannot be filed sooner than SEVEN YEARS after the conditional dismissal or the setting aside of the judgment. The petition, proposed order and declaration in this packet are for exactly this branch.

BARRED ON BOTH BRANCHES: subsection 3 of each section forbids sealing under the section where you were charged with a violation of NRS 200.508 (abuse, neglect or endangerment of a child) or NRS 200.5099 (abuse, neglect, exploitation, isolation or abandonment of an older person or a vulnerable person). If that was the charge, stop: nothing in this packet can be filed, and a lawyer or Nevada Legal Services is the place to take the question.

Sealing under these sections is also not available where the programme was not completed and you were sentenced rather than discharged or the case dismissed.

sections.heading: Check the discharge in the court record
sections.body:
If you were discharged from probation, was the discharge HONOURABLE or DISHONOURABLE?

On this track the answer does not change the mechanism: subsections 1 and 2 turn on whether you fulfilled the terms and conditions imposed by the court and the Division, not on a presumption.

It matters for what comes after. NRS 179.2445(2) provides that the rebuttable presumption in favour of sealing does NOT apply to a defendant given a dishonorable discharge from probation under NRS 176A.850 who applies for sealing of records relating to the conviction. If your discharge was dishonourable, any later petition on the ordinary conviction track under NRS 179.245 proceeds without that presumption, and that is a reason to talk to a lawyer or Nevada Legal Services before filing anything anywhere.

Your own court paperwork states which discharge you were given; the clerk of the court that handled the case can confirm it from the record.

documents.title: Petition to Seal Records Under Subsection 2 of NRS 176A.245, 176A.265 or 176A.295
documents.conditionDescription: Generated only on the subsection 2 branch: a violation of NRS 200.485, NRS 484C.110 or NRS 484C.120, conditionally dismissed or the judgment of conviction set aside, and not sooner than seven years after.

sections.heading: Use restriction
sections.body: USE THIS PETITION ONLY ON THE SUBSECTION 2 BRANCH: you were charged with a violation of NRS 200.485, NRS 484C.110 or NRS 484C.120, the charges were conditionally dismissed or the judgment of conviction set aside, and not sooner than seven years have passed since. On the subsection 1 branch nothing is filed — the branch-screen page of this packet is the test.

assertions.text: The petitioner, {{participant_full_legal_name}}, petitions this Court, as the court that handled the case identified above, to order sealed all records relating to that case, as subsection 2 of the applicable section provides.
The petitioner states, from the court's own records:
Not sooner than seven years have elapsed since the date stated above, as subsection 2 requires.
The petitioner fulfilled the terms and conditions imposed by the court and by the Division of Parole and Probation.
The petitioner was not charged with a violation of NRS 200.508 or NRS 200.5099, which subsection 3 of each section excludes from sealing.

The petitioner therefore asks the Court to order sealed all documents, papers and exhibits in the petitioner's record, minute book entries and entries on dockets, and other documents relating to the case in the custody of the agencies and officers named in the proposed order submitted with this petition, as subsection 2 of the applicable section provides. The petitioner is advised that the court shall order the records sealed without a hearing unless the Division petitions the court, for good cause shown, not to seal the records and requests a hearing thereon.

sections.heading: How to complete this order
sections.body: This proposed order accompanies the subsection 2 petition. The list of agencies and officers below is operative text, not formality: subsections 1 and 2 reach only records "in the custody of such other agencies and officers as are named in the court's order", and under subsection 4 each named agency or officer must notify the court in writing of compliance. You list every agency that touched your case, from your own papers.

captionContract.courtInstruction: THE SAME COURT AS THE PETITION
captionContract.matterTitle: IN THE MATTER OF THE PETITION OF {{participant_full_legal_name}} TO SEAL RECORDS

captionContract.documentTitle: ORDER SEALING RECORDS UNDER SUBSECTION 2 OF NRS 176A.245, NRS 176A.265 OR NRS 176A.295

sections.heading: Agencies and officers whose records are sealed
sections.body:
The petition of the above-named petitioner to seal records having been filed under subsection 2 of the applicable section, and the Division not having petitioned the court, for good cause shown, not to seal the records,

IT IS ORDERED that all documents, papers and exhibits in the petitioner's record, minute book entries and entries on dockets, and other documents relating to the case in the custody of the agencies and officers named below are SEALED.

fieldLabels.named_agencies_and_officers: Agencies and officers whose records are sealed by this order (listed by the petitioner from the petitioner's own papers; every agency that touched the case belongs on these lines)

sections.heading: Distribution of the order
sections.body: Under subsection 4 of the applicable section, the court will send a copy of this order to each agency or officer named in it, and each must notify the court in writing of compliance. Under NRS 179.275 a copy also goes to the Central Repository for Nevada Records of Criminal History.

sections.body: This declaration accompanies the subsection 2 petition. The sections prescribe no verification; this is the ordinary support for facts not appearing of record, and every fact on it is yours to state from your own records.

assertions.text: I, {{participant_full_legal_name}}, am the petitioner in the accompanying petition to seal records.
The case ran under the chapter 176A programme stated below, and I completed it:
The charge was resolved as stated below — conditionally dismissed, or the judgment of conviction set aside — on the date stated below:
Not sooner than seven years have elapsed since that date. The computation is mine, made from the date on my own court paperwork.
I fulfilled the terms and conditions imposed by the court and by the Division of Parole and Probation.
I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.

feeAndWaiver.statement: NRS 176A.245, NRS 176A.265, and NRS 176A.295 prescribe no fee. Before filing a subsection 2 petition, ask the clerk whether that court charges a filing fee; this specification states no amount.

serviceAndNotice.statement: The sections prescribe no participant service on either branch. On subsection 1 there is nothing to serve. After an order, the court sends it to each named agency or officer, and a copy also goes to the Central Repository under NRS 179.275.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The charge was under NRS 200.508 or NRS 200.5099.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Subsection 3 bars sealing under these sections on both branches.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The Division petitions for good cause not to seal and requests a hearing.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: That is a contested proceeding; stop and get legal help.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: Whether the participant fulfilled the terms and conditions imposed by the court and the Division is disputed or unclear.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Both branches turn on that condition, so the packet cannot resolve the dispute.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The program was not completed and the participant was sentenced rather than discharged or the case dismissed.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Sealing under these sections is not available on the approved route record.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The seven-year period has not elapsed or its start date is uncertain.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The subsection 2 petition cannot be filed before the period elapses, and the record must establish the disposition and date.
NRS 179.2445(2) removes the presumption on a later NRS 179.245 petition; get help before using an ordinary conviction route.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: Records are in more than one county or court, or federal, tribal, military, or out-of-state records are involved.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Court practice or the reach of a Nevada order is outside this packet's self-help scope.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: There is a pending charge, an offence-category question, a firearm-rights goal, or an immigration question.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Those issues require individualized legal advice and are outside this packet's self-help scope.

participantChecklist.text: Case number and the identity of the court that handled the case — Petition caption, on the subsection 2 branch only.
The list of agencies and officers to be named in the sealing order — Proposed order, on the subsection 2 branch only.
Signature and date — Petition and declaration, on the subsection 2 branch only.
On the subsection 2 branch the petitioner signs the petition and the declaration personally. On the subsection 1 branch nothing is generated for the participant to sign.
None required. The sections prescribe no verification or notarization.

None is prescribed. Neither NRS 176A.245, NRS 176A.265 nor NRS 176A.295 imposes, authorises or mentions a fee, on either branch. Whether a particular clerk charges a filing fee for the subsection 2 petition is not established by the sections and is recorded as an open question rather than asserted either way. The NRS 179.245(9) sex-trafficking fee waiver is confined by its own words to a petition for sealing under NRS 179.245 and does not by its terms reach these sections.

None prescribed by these sections. NRS 179.245(9) waives fees related to a petition for sealing under NRS 179.245 where the petitioner was being sex trafficked when the crime was committed; its text is confined to that section and it is not authority for a waiver here.
Before filing on subsection 2, ask the clerk whether the petition must be served on the Division of Parole and Probation or the prosecutor; the sections prescribe no participant service.
File a subsection 2 petition in the justice, municipal, or district court that handled the case; file nothing on subsection 1.
